title: Key-value command interpreter
prompt:
Add `execute(line, store)` in a new module `app/commands.py`. `line` is a command string whose words are separated by whitespace, and `store` is a dict that the commands read and change. `execute` returns a string. Raise `CommandError` (already in `app/errors.py`) for every error. Command names are case-insensitive. Commands:
- `set KEY VALUE...` stores the remaining words joined by single spaces; returns "OK".
- `get KEY` returns the value; a missing key is an error.
- `del KEY` removes the key and returns "1", or returns "0" if it did not exist.
- `exists KEY` returns "1" or "0".
- `incr KEY [N]` and `decr KEY [N]` add or subtract N (default 1) to the integer stored at KEY (a missing key counts as 0) and return the new value; a stored value or N that is not an integer is an error.
- `append KEY TEXT...` appends the remaining words joined by single spaces to the value (a missing key counts as an empty string) and returns the new length.
- `rename OLD NEW` moves a value; OLD must exist and NEW must not exist; returns "OK".
- `swap A B` exchanges the values of two existing keys; returns "OK".
- `keys [PREFIX]` returns the matching keys sorted and joined by single spaces, or "(empty)" if there are none.
- `count` returns the number of keys; `clear` removes all keys and returns "OK".
Errors and their exact messages: an empty line -> "empty command"; an unknown command -> "unknown command: NAME" (NAME as typed); the wrong number of arguments -> "wrong number of arguments for NAME" (NAME lowercase); a missing key -> "no such key: KEY"; a stored value or N that is not an integer -> "not an integer: X" (X is the offending text); renaming onto an existing key -> "key exists: NEW".
Add tests in `tests/test_commands.py`. Run the tests with `python -m pytest -q`, and when they pass commit your work with git.
